2025 California Electrical Code Updates for San Marino Properties

San Marino property owners must stay current with the latest electrical code requirements to ensure safety, maintain property values, and avoid potential compliance issues. The 2025 California Electrical Code, based on the NFPA 70 2023 edition with California-specific amendments, introduces several critical updates that affect both residential and commercial properties throughout Los Angeles County, including San Marino.

One of the most significant changes involves expanded GFCI (Ground-Fault Circuit Interrupter) protection requirements. The updated code now requires GFCI protection for a broader range of appliances and locations, including wall-mounted ovens, counter-mounted cooking units, clothes dryers, and microwave ovens. Additionally, the previous distance limitation between kitchen receptacle outlets and sinks has been removed, meaning any cord-and-plug-connected appliance in kitchens now requires GFCI protection. These changes significantly enhance electrical safety in San Marino homes, reducing the risk of electrical shock in areas where water and electricity may come into contact.

Shaffer Construction stays at the forefront of these code changes, ensuring that all electrical work performed on San Marino properties meets or exceeds current requirements. Our electricians receive ongoing training on code updates and best practices, providing homeowners with peace of mind that their electrical systems are both safe and compliant. Beyond GFCI requirements, the 2025 code also mandates tamper-resistant outlets in all habitable areas, representing a shift from viewing these as merely childproofing measures to recognizing them as essential general safety standards.

Another important update addresses emergency disconnects for dwelling units. The code now requires outside emergency disconnects for feeders supplied to one- and two-family dwelling units, ensuring that first responders can always shut off power from the exterior of a building regardless of how it is supplied. For San Marino's many historic and custom homes, Shaffer Construction carefully integrates these required disconnects in ways that maintain architectural aesthetics while ensuring full code compliance and emergency access.

EV Charger Installation: Meeting Modern Transportation Needs

Electric vehicle adoption continues to accelerate across Los Angeles County, and San Marino residents are increasingly making the switch to electric transportation. According to the U.S. Department of Energy's National EV Charging Network initiative, the number of public EV charging ports in the United States has grown more than six-fold over the last decade, from approximately 30,000 in 2016 to nearly 196,000 in January 2025. This growth reflects the rapidly expanding EV market and the critical need for reliable charging infrastructure.

For San Marino homeowners, installing a Level 2 EV charger at home provides the convenience of overnight charging and eliminates the need to rely solely on public charging infrastructure. Shaffer Construction specializes in residential EV charger installation, handling every aspect of the project from initial electrical assessment to final testing and certification. Our comprehensive approach ensures that your home's electrical system can safely support the additional load while maintaining efficiency and reliability for all other electrical needs.

California's building code requirements for EV charging infrastructure have become increasingly stringent. The Alternative Fuels Data Center reports that new one- and two-unit single-family dwellings or townhouses with attached private garages must have an electrical conduit installed capable of supporting a Level 2 EV charger. While this requirement applies to new construction, many existing San Marino homes require electrical upgrades to support EV charging equipment safely and effectively.

As we discussed in our guide to planning EV charger infrastructure installation in Los Angeles, proper planning is essential for successful EV charger installation. Shaffer Construction begins every EV charger project with a thorough electrical assessment, evaluating your existing service panel capacity, determining whether upgrades are necessary, and identifying the optimal location for your charging equipment. Our electricians are experienced with all major EV charger brands and can recommend solutions that match your specific vehicle requirements and usage patterns.

Electrical Panel Upgrades: Supporting Growing Power Demands

Many San Marino homes, particularly those built several decades ago, were originally equipped with 100-amp electrical service panels designed for the power consumption patterns of that era. Today's homes place significantly greater demands on electrical systems, with multiple high-powered appliances, advanced HVAC systems, home offices filled with electronics, and increasingly, electric vehicle charging equipment. When electrical demand exceeds panel capacity, homeowners may experience frequent circuit breaker trips, dimming lights, or even potential safety hazards.

Upgrading to a 200-amp service panel is often the most practical solution for San Marino homeowners looking to modernize their electrical infrastructure. This upgrade provides the capacity needed to support current and future electrical demands while maintaining safety and reliability. Shaffer Construction has completed countless panel upgrade projects throughout Los Angeles County, working with both the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power and local utility providers to ensure seamless installation and activation of upgraded electrical service.

The process of upgrading an electrical panel involves several critical steps. First, our electricians conduct a comprehensive load study to determine your home's actual power requirements and identify the appropriate panel size for your needs. Our electrical load studies take into account not only your current electrical usage but also anticipated future needs, such as EV charging, solar power integration, or home additions. This forward-thinking approach ensures that your upgraded panel will serve your needs for years to come without requiring additional costly upgrades.

Once the load study is complete, Shaffer Construction handles all aspects of the panel upgrade, including obtaining necessary permits from San Marino's building department, coordinating with your utility company for temporary power disconnection and service upgrades, installing the new panel and associated components, and arranging for final inspections to ensure code compliance. Throughout the process, we maintain clear communication with homeowners, minimizing disruption and ensuring you understand each step of the project.

Safety Inspections and Code Compliance

Electrical safety should never be taken for granted, particularly in older homes or properties that have undergone multiple renovations over the years. Shaffer Construction offers comprehensive electrical safety inspections for San Marino properties, identifying potential hazards, code violations, and opportunities for improvement. These inspections are particularly valuable for homeowners purchasing older properties, preparing homes for sale, or simply seeking peace of mind about their electrical system's safety and reliability.

During a thorough electrical safety inspection, our licensed electricians examine every aspect of your electrical system, including the service panel and main breaker, all branch circuits and circuit breakers, outlets and switches throughout the home, GFCI and AFCI protection devices, grounding systems, lighting fixtures, and any specialized electrical equipment or systems. We document our findings in a detailed report that identifies any safety concerns, code violations, or recommended improvements, prioritized by urgency and importance.

The 2023 National Electrical Code updates implemented in California include important safety provisions that may not have been required when older homes were built. For example, AFCI (Arc-Fault Circuit Interrupter) protection, now required in various locations including sleeping areas, helps prevent electrical fires by detecting dangerous arc-faults in electrical wiring. Shaffer Construction can retrofit existing homes with these modern safety features, bringing older electrical systems up to current safety standards even when not strictly required by code.

For San Marino homeowners, maintaining code compliance is not just about meeting legal requirements; it is also about protecting your investment, ensuring your family's safety, and maintaining insurability. Many insurance companies now require electrical inspections for older homes or may offer premium discounts for homes with updated, code-compliant electrical systems. Shaffer Construction works closely with homeowners, real estate professionals, and insurance companies to provide the documentation and assurances needed throughout the property transaction and ownership experience.
